criteria.rubric: One independently testable audio subsystem owns packet parsing, formats, clocks, sample timing, DSP and buffer operations; the core loop uses buffers without direct device IO.
The adjacent device gateway owns physical device abstractions and lifecycle; playback evidence distinguishes actual consumption from queue admission.
A separate Go module constructs and exercises the runtime without CLI imports, flags, terminal state or hidden global initialization.
Services expose thin services/X contracts with private services/X/internal implementations and per-service Wire construction; CLI transport delegates business behavior.
Correlated device capture/playback, provider send/receive, tool lifecycle, cancellation, queues/drops and terminal evidence use explicit timing domains and bounded recording resources.
Credential-free replay preserves recorded audio packets, ordering, tool events, interruption and termination; hardware and external nondeterminism limits are explicit.

Truncated/no playback, barge-in failure, long-conversation slowdown and tool-continuation collisions have reproducible characterization, fixes where demonstrated, and exact residual limitations without false completion claims.

Architecture boundaries, package/file/function size, complexity, mutable globals, generated Wire consistency and relevant compile/static/race checks pass without growing migration baselines or weakening assertions.

Supported CLI behavior is preserved and final integrated behavior has fresh independent customer and engineering evidence, with authorized bounded Realtime proof and explicit physical-device evidence limits.

help.stdout:
Yui is a cross-platform voice-agent CLI for realtime conversations, local tools, recordings, replay, and structured WebMCP browser control.

Set an OpenAI key, then start the default microphone and speaker session:

  export OPENAI_API_KEY="your-openai-api-key"
  yui session

Run `yui session --help` for audio, model, voice, recording, and browser options.

Usage:
  yui [command]

Examples:
  # Start a voice session in the current project
  yui --workdir "$PWD" session

  # Open a page and expose its WebMCP tools
  yui session --browser-tools webmcp --browser-open https://example.com/

Available Commands:
  ask         Ask the agent a question and get a response
  chat        Start an interactive chat session with the agent
  completion  Generate the autocompletion script for the specified shell
  config      Configuration management commands
  devices     Discover available audio devices
  help        Help about any command
  interaction Inspect provider-neutral gateway interactions
  media       Inspect external media sources
  probe       Run deterministic offline probes
  room        Run participant rooms
  session     Run or manage agent sessions
  tool        Invoke a tool directly by name and key=value args (for debugging)
  webmcp      Inspect WebMCP browser readiness

Flags:
      --allow-path stringArray   Additional filesystem-tool root (repeatable; relative to --workdir)
  -C, --config-dir string        Directory for agent CLI config (default: ~/.agent-cli)
  -h, --help                     help for yui
      --log-to-stdout            Log to stdout/stderr instead of file (default: logs to file in config directory)
  -v, --verbose count            Enable verbose output (use -v for info, -vv for debug)
      --workdir string           Filesystem-tool workdir (default: the process current directory)

Use "yui [command] --help" for more information about a command.
